    Finite-dimensional modules are finitely presented with respect to F #

    A homomorphism from a finite-dimensional A-module into F(X) factors through some Φ(U), and two such factorizations agree at a later stage. This is the finite presentation used in the proofs of Proposition 2.5 and Theorem 2.7. The algebra A is finite-dimensional.

    ∃ (U' : Kron.FinSub X), U₀ ≤ U' ∧ ∀ (i : ι), U i ≤ U'

    Finitely many finite-dimensional subrepresentations have a common upper bound above a given one.
